english: a friend in need is a friend indeed

terms.latin: Is est amīcus quī in rē dubiā rē juvat, ubi rēst opus.
evidence: Plaut. Epid. 113: is est amīcus, quī in rē dubiā rē juvat, ubi rēst opus
terms.comment: Literally “he is a friend who helps in deed in a doubtful matter, when there is need of it”. A line of Plautus; rēst is rē est run together, as it was spoken. Traupman gives the line without its end.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 255.
